issues.title: Join min/max + BF pushdown through CM compress projections (q09)
issues.hypothesis: In q09 the orders scan reads all 15M rows for the o_orderkey hash join, because the join filter pushdown stops at __internal_compress_integral_* projections that compressed materialization inserts. A prior run measured: offset-aware min/max (+off) and BF (hash of (x-off) masked to key width) cut the orders scan from 15M to 2.96M rows, q09 -8.2%. The current best now has BF on the first key of multi-key HJ (E0005), so more joins in q09 have a BF to push.
issues.plan: In src/optimizer/join_filter_pushdown_optimizer.cpp, follow bindings through projections whose expression is __internal_compress_integral_*(col, const_offset), and record the offset in JoinFilterPushdownColumn (join_filter_pushdown.hpp). In physical_hash_join.cpp (JoinFilterPushdownInfo::FinalizeFilters / PushBloomFilter), add the offset to min/max constants, and for the BF hash the probe value the way the build side does. Simplest: only push the BF when the build key is itself the compressed value, or skip the BF when offset != 0, and push min/max only. TopN optimizer and RowGroupPruner also call GetPushdownFilterTargets, so they must reject columns with an offset. If the q18 key-set issue landed first, reuse its offset plumbing.
issues.generality: Any join whose probe key passes through a compressed-materialization projection, which is common whenever an aggregate or sort sits between the scan and the join.
issues.risk: Medium. An offset applied wrongly causes wrong pruning, so test with an offset-shifted key range against a col+0 variant.

dispatch: Join key-set range filter through compress projections

## Memory (gen1)

## State
- r1: E0001 JoinDependentFilterRule before DistributivityRule ACCEPTED: q19 -46%, geomean -4.2%.
- r2: E0002 contains()/LIKE length-aware selectivity ACCEPTED: q09 -37%, geomean -3.9%.
- r3: E0003 Perfect HJ RIGHT v2 ACCEPTED: q13 -18..-20%. Large range (up to 4M) is allowed only for RIGHT joins; for INNER it regressed q14 +52% and q18 +13% (serial perfect build, no BF).
- r4: E0004 substring prefilter (ColumnData::Filter) RETIRED. q13 -7.7% (needed -13.8%), q09 -5..-8%. A good idea that fell short of the bar; retry it bundled with FSST batched decode or the follow-ups (multi-segment match, rarest segment as needle).
- r5: E0005 BF on first key of multi-key HJ ACCEPTED: q09 -18..-22%. Best 1.106x. Follow-up: BF on the most selective key, or one BF per key.
- r6 DISPATCHED: Join key-set range filter through compress projs (q18 -13.6% prior). Filed: min/max+BF through CM compress for q09 (-8% prior); it can reuse the offset plumbing from r6.
- Current top templates: q18 697ms (16.3%), q13 645, q09 628, q04 294, q05 281, q03 257.
- Claude auto-memory (~/.claude/.../memory) holds results from a PREVIOUS evolve run on this same codebase/workload. Treat them as strong measured priors, not as already-landed code. Read the specific memory .md files directly with Read.

## Prior-run wins to port, in rough priority order (gain / risk)
1-4. DONE (rule reorder, contains selectivity, perfect HJ RIGHT, BF first key).
5. r6: q18 key-set range filter. Then semi-join RHS-aware estimate (q18 -8%).
6. q09: join filter through CM compress (-8%), exact BF through CM offset (-14%), exact bitmap BF for dense int keys (q09/q16/q21 -10..-15%).
7. Large perfect HA (22-bit) + parallel source: q13 -18.6%. Distinct HT partitioned on group hash: q16 -12%.
8. OR-of-ranges as ExpressionFilter, dense mask eval: q19 -7..-11%.
9. FSST batched decode (q13 -4..-7%), possibly combined with the substring prefilter retry.
10. Follow-up from E0003: parallel perfect HJ build, or keep the BF alongside it, which would unlock large-range INNER perfect HJ.
- q04 (294ms) and q03 have no prior idea; profile them once the ports run out.

## Known dead ends (prior run)
- HJ prefetch, agg run-collapse, in-place finalize, FSST heap reuse, dictionary filter, scan filter cost ordering, early HT grow, sparse perfect HJ, bitpacking select: all ~0%.

## Codebase facts
- Rule registration order lives in src/optimizer/optimizer.cpp.
- Scan-filter cardinality: RelationStatisticsHelper::InspectTableFilter (relation_statistics_helper.cpp).
- ColumnData::Filter = Scan + ColumnSegment::FilterSelection. enable_fsst_vectors defaults to false.
- Perfect HJ gates: perfect_hash_join_executor.cpp CanDoPerfectHashJoin; join_filter_pushdown_optimizer.cpp computes min/max aggregates.
- BF pushdown: physical_hash_join.cpp JoinFilterPushdownInfo::FinalizeFilters (deferred_bloom_filters). The BF is skipped when has_cast or when there is a perfect HT. E0005 added InsertFirstKeyIntoBloomFilter in join_hashtable.cpp Finalize.
- JoinFilterPushdownColumn is in include/duckdb/execution/operator/join/join_filter_pushdown.hpp. CM functions are in src/function/scalar/compressed_materialization/compress_integral.cpp.
- CM runs in STATISTICS_PROPAGATION, after TopN/RowGroupPruner. Those also call GetPushdownFilterTargets, so they must reject columns with an offset.
- Noise: q04/q08 swing ±7-15% (run-order dependent); q13 needs about -14% to count. Single-template gains under ~10% tend to get retired.
- Testing NOT LIKE pushdown: compare against s||'' (not concat). Testing BF: compare against a col+0=col+0 variant.
- Budget is tight (~$4/session): read memory/ledger, then dispatch the next prior win quickly.
